task_description: Write a method in Dafny to compute the n-th power of each number in a list.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method PowerEachElementInList(lst: seq<int>, n: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The result list should have the same length as the input list
    - For each index i in 0 .. |lst| - 1, result[i] should be lst[i] raised to the power n
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method PowerList(l: seq<int>, n: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The exponent n should be non-negative
    
Dafny specification:
    requires n >= 0
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result sequence has the same length as the input list
    - Each element in the result sequence is the corresponding element in the input list raised to the power n

Dafny specification:
    ensures |result| == |l|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |l| ==> result[i] == Power(l[i], n)
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method PowerList(l: seq<int>, n: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires n >= 0
    ensures |result| == |l|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |l| ==> result[i] == Power(l[i], n)
{
    result := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < |l|
        invariant 0 <= i <= |l|
        invariant |result| == i
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == Power(l[j], n)
    {
        result := result + [Power(l[i], n)];
        i := i + 1;
    }
}

// Auxiliary function for exponentiation
function Power(base: int, exp: int): int
    requires exp >= 0
{
    if exp == 0 then 1
    else base * Power(base, exp - 1)
}
```
